questions.prompt: Neither the manager nor his assistants ______ available at the moment.
questions.explanation: With 'neither ... nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'Assistants' is plural, so 'are' is correct.

questions.prompt: By the time the police arrived, the thieves ______.
questions.explanation: The past perfect ('had fled') marks an action completed before another past action ('arrived').

questions.prompt: One of the students ______ lost his book.
questions.explanation: 'One of the + plural noun' takes a singular verb: the subject is 'one', not 'students'.

questions.prompt: She ______ in this office since 2015.
questions.explanation: 'Since + a point in time' with an action continuing into the present takes the present perfect continuous.

questions.prompt: If he ______ harder, he would have passed the examination.
questions.explanation: Third conditional: 'If + past perfect, ... would have + past participle' for an unreal past condition.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct passive form of: 'The secretary typed the letter yesterday.'
choices: The letter is typed by the secretary yesterday.
The letter was typed by the secretary yesterday.
The letter has been typed by the secretary yesterday.
The letter was being typed by the secretary yesterday.
questions.explanation: The simple past active becomes 'was/were + past participle' in the passive: 'was typed'.

questions.prompt: The committee ______ divided in its opinion on the new policy.
questions.explanation: The collective noun is treated as a single body here - signalled by 'its' - so the singular 'is' agrees.

questions.prompt: He was accused ______ theft.
questions.explanation: The fixed collocation is 'accused of' (compare: 'charged with').

questions.prompt: ______ honest man is respected everywhere.
questions.explanation: 'Honest' begins with a silent 'h', so it opens with a vowel sound and takes 'an'.

questions.prompt: He is superior ______ me in intelligence.
questions.explanation: Latin comparatives - superior, inferior, senior, junior, prior - take 'to', never 'than'.

questions.prompt: The teacher distributed the sweets ______ the five children.
questions.explanation: 'Between' is used for two parties; 'among' for more than two.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
choices: Each of the boys have submitted their assignment.
Each of the boys has submitted his assignment.
Each of the boy has submitted their assignment.
Each of the boys are submitting their assignment.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular, so it takes 'has' and a singular pronoun, while the noun after 'of' stays plural.

questions.prompt: She has been suffering ______ fever for three days.
questions.explanation: One suffers 'from' an illness; 'die of' and 'suffer from' are the standard collocations.

questions.prompt: I congratulated him ______ his brilliant success.
questions.explanation: The verb 'congratulate' takes 'on' before the achievement.

questions.prompt: Choose the word closest in meaning to UBIQUITOUS:
questions.explanation: Ubiquitous = present everywhere at once, i.e. omnipresent.

questions.prompt: Choose the word closest in meaning to CANDID:
questions.explanation: Candid means open and straightforward in speech - frank.

questions.prompt: Choose the OPPOSITE of FRUGAL:
questions.explanation: Frugal means sparing with money; its opposite is extravagant. Thrifty and economical are synonyms of it.

questions.prompt: Choose the OPPOSITE of BENEVOLENT:
questions.explanation: Benevolent (well-wishing) is the direct opposite of malevolent (ill-wishing).

questions.prompt: Choose the word closest in meaning to ALLEVIATE:
questions.explanation: To alleviate is to make pain or a burden less severe - to relieve. 'Aggravate' is its opposite.

questions.prompt: Choose the OPPOSITE of TRANSPARENT:
questions.explanation: Opaque - not allowing light to pass through - is the antonym of transparent.

questions.prompt: Choose the word closest in meaning to METICULOUS:
questions.explanation: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail - painstaking, scrupulous.

questions.prompt: 'To bury the hatchet' means:
questions.explanation: From the custom of burying weapons when hostilities ended - to settle a quarrel.

questions.prompt: 'A blessing in disguise' means:
choices: Something that seems bad but turns out to be good
questions.explanation: An apparent misfortune whose benefit only becomes clear later.

questions.prompt: The match was called ______ because of rain.
questions.explanation: 'Call off' = cancel. 'Call on' = visit; 'call up' = telephone or summon.

questions.prompt: 'To beat about the bush' means:
choices: To avoid coming to the main point
questions.explanation: To approach a subject indirectly instead of addressing it head-on.

questions.prompt: I cannot put up ______ his rude behaviour any longer.
questions.explanation: 'Put up with' means to tolerate or endure.

questions.prompt: 'To turn a deaf ear' means:
questions.explanation: To deliberately ignore what someone says or asks for.

questions.prompt: 'Once in a blue moon' means:
questions.explanation: A blue moon is an uncommon event, so the idiom means 'very seldom'.
